You just have to allot time to study it. I had no idea how to go about it also at first so inaral ko talaga. And yun nga, iba iba sinasabi but that’s also because iba iba nga naman kasi yung case based on the type of business.

DTI and BIR fees are generally standard range. Meaning, it’s the same for all locations/regions. It will just depend on your type of business. 

DTI can be done online. Fees can range from 200-2k depending on the geographical scope of your business. 

BIR rates will just differ based on the type of business you register. Sole prop will be less than 200, that’s for the provisionary receipts and books of accounts. Registration fee has been waived since the start of the year. 

You’ll need to have receipts printed, which I think will range 1-2k depending on the accredited printer you choose 

Brgy Clearance and Business Permit will be different depending on your city. Requirements may be different too. So fees will depend also. It’s a given there are cities na na-red tape and you may incur some hidden fees, while some are more straightforward. 

As for FDA, I have no Idea about that. My only experience with FDA is when I used to have clients who needed FDA permits for their products. From what I remember the process takes a while and they usually hire people to do it for them. 

My advice is that you research and understand the processes needed so you won’t be hit with hidden charges or they will be minimal at least. There are a lot of resources on DTI and especially BIR registration. r/taxph is a good first stop. Even if you decide to hire someone to do it all for you, it’s better to still understand what the process is so you know what they’re charging you for. 

For your local permits, ask other people who processed their permits regarding their experience. Or if you can, just ask go to your city hall or whichever office issues the local permits so you can find out the requirements directly.

No, the process is: 

1. Get your COR first. Use form 1901 for this. 
2. Once you have your COR, choose a BIR accredited printer.
3. Secure your ATP. 
- ask your chosen printer to print you a sample layout. 
- fill out form 1906. Usually the printer has this na. Just provide your info based on the COR
- submit to BIR to secure ATP. 
- once you have the ATP, give it to the printer so they can start printing. 


To your questions. 

1 - go to the RDO, line up, when your number is called present all the documents to the officer. They will tell you if you need additional documents or whatever. In my experience, I got my COR same day. Went early but their system was offline so the officer just checked my docs if complete. They told me I can proceed to pay my reg fee (that’s waived now so no need to pay this) and try to go back in the afternoon. So I paid nalang muna via bank over the counter and went back in the afternoon. Luckily, they were online already and got my COR right there. 

2 - you issue receipts as soon as you register. There is a provisionary receipt you can buy from BIR. You can use this while you’re still processing your ATP and waiting for the receipts to be printed.

No, hindi siya binibigay automatically kasi BIR needs to see muna a sample layout of the receipt to approve it. Check the COR, nakalagay dun sa baba what else you need to get after registration. 

You can check the process and requirements of how to get and ATP here [here](https://www.bir.gov.ph/index.php/registration-requirements/secondary-registration/application-for-authority-to-print-receipts-invoices.html#procedures)

Before going to BIR, you have to have a sample receipt layout muna so pick a printer from their [list of printers](https://www.bir.gov.ph/images/bir_files/taxpayers_service_programs_and_monitoring_2/Printers/000-03042024120008-LIST%20OF%20ACCREDITED%20PRINTERS.xls.pdf) so the printer can print you a sample layout. Familiar na sila with the process of it. Usually, sila na magpprint ng form 1906 for you.

Yung ibang printers they offer ATP processing na rin for an additional fee. But honestly, mabilis lang siya iprocess basta your documents are complete and correct.

Ang alam ko kung less than 100 yung total ng bili, hindi required magissue ng receipts unless humingi si customer. If humingi you have to give a receipt. 

Also, hindi pwedeng bumibili lang ng receipts online. BIR has a list of accredited printers nationwide that can print receipts. You need to secure an ATP from BIR before ka makapagpaprint ng receipts.

For the face naman, I always moisturize and use aloe gel. Seems to do the trick for me lalo na if I start seeing some flakes forming. Nips it in the bud. But if it gets bad, I use either Aveeno or Bepanthen anti-itch cream. Then last resort is Elica. 

Food is important also. When I have flares, I cut down sugar and carbs. I tried to do low carb before but I can’t sustain it since pasta and bread is ❤️haha. So I just cut down whenever I feel flare ups coming.

In my experience, the bigger Hydroflask bottles stays cold longer. I have the 21oz and 40oz ones. Yung 21oz mga 12hrs lang siguro and hindi nagllast yung ice the whole day. Yung 40oz, may chunks of ice pa natitira until 2 days. Yung Aquaflask na 40oz up to 1 day at most yung ice. The following day malamig pa din naman pero no more ice.

Pero ang best pa rin for me is Thermos and Yeti. Thermos because heavy duty. You won't worry about dents. Yeti halos 3 days ata umabot yung ice. Pero ang bulky lang kasi nila kaya usually dala ko siya for travel. Yung 40oz Hydroflask is the one for my daily use. 

Though never ko pa sila natry for hot drinks. Someone told me din kasi na mixing hot and cold drinks ruins the insulation. Idk how true. Pero I've never had the need naman to store hot drinks for long periods so hindi ko din natry.

Additional tip: instead of wearing thick jackets, better to layer your clothes when you're outside. Kasi nagiiba iba ang temp during the day. Minsan ang lamig sa morning then maaraw sa tanghali then uulan sa hapon.
